pages.title: Features
pages.content:
\ Five things, in this order /

Everything the week needs

Wariate Shifts is rota software for shops: lay out the week, collect availability, swap shifts, cover sick days, and turn hours over for payroll. Each part below is the same work we walk through in the demo hour, in the same order.

\ Feature 1 of 5 /

Lay out the week

Lay out the week

Collect availability

Swap a shift

Cover a sick day

Hours for payroll

Lay out the week

The week starts from the sheet you already keep. Copy last week's pattern, then drag people into the gaps the new week opens. When the grid looks right, publish it to everyone's phone.

A manager who has written the rota by hand usually knows the shape before sitting down: who opens, who closes, which days the part-timers can take. The pattern holds that memory, so you change only what changed. Staff read the published week on their own phones.

If the floor still wants paper, the same week can be printed and pinned by the staff door. In the demo this is minutes 10 to 35. We enter your real sheet together and lay out next week.

The pass does not ask you to learn a new way of thinking about the rota. It puts the week you already understand where the team can see it before the shutters go up.

\ Feature 2 of 5 /

Collect availability

Lay out the week

Collect availability

Swap a shift

Cover a sick day

Hours for payroll

Collect availability

Staff mark the days they can work. A reminder goes out on Thursday. Answers land on the rota grid.

You are not pulling replies out of a group chat and copying names across by hand. The reminder is one message, on the same weekday, which suits a shop that opens before 08:00 and does not want another thread running into the weekend. You still decide the week.

An answer is information on the grid, not a claim that every request can be met. When a season needs extra hands, the same three steps collect those days first, so the busy Saturdays are laid out before the ordinary week is filled. In the demo, an availability request is one of the live changes between minutes 35 and 50.

You see the reminder, the reply, and the grid update in the same hour, using your own staff and your own week.

\ Feature 3 of 5 /

Swap a shift

Lay out the week

Collect availability

Swap a shift

Cover a sick day

Hours for payroll

Swap a shift

A colleague offers a shift. Another accepts. You approve once.

The offer stays between the people who work that week, and the rota does not change until you say so. That path replaces the Friday phone call that used to fix a weekend early shift after the shop had already closed. At Hollin Bakery the weekend early shift, on a shop that opens at 06:30, used to be settled that way.

Now the staff swap it among themselves and Ines Duarte approves once. The same path works for a late close or a midweek gap. Both people can see the shift on their phones before anyone accepts, and you see the offer and the acceptance together.

In the demo we run one swap live, between minutes 35 and 50, so you can watch the approval land on the grid without the rest of the week being rebuilt.

\ Feature 4 of 5 /

Cover a sick day

Lay out the week

Collect availability

Swap a shift

Cover a sick day

Hours for payroll

Cover a sick day

Mark the shift open. Free, qualified people are asked. The first yes fills it.

You do not start a fresh phone round while the shutters are coming up. The open shift goes to people who are free that day and already able to do the work, and the first yes writes the name back onto the grid. You still see who was asked and who filled it.

A sick day is one of the three changes we run in the demo, in minutes 35 to 50, after the availability request and the swap. The point of doing it live is so you can see that the rest of the week stays put. One open shift is filled.

Neighbouring shifts are not rebuilt unless you move them. Shops with many part-timers often have more than one person who could cover. The ask goes to those people, not to the whole staff list.

\ Feature 5 of 5 /

Hours for payroll

Lay out the week

Collect availability

Swap a shift

Cover a sick day

Hours for payroll

Hours for payroll

Clock in at the counter. Breaks are added up. Export the week by Sunday night.

The hours follow the same grid you published, so the figure you hand across is the week the floor actually worked, with breaks included. This is not a payroll system. It does not calculate pay, tax or deductions, and it is not a replacement for the payroll you already run.

It gives you the hours, ready to export, on Sunday night, while the week is still clear. Support is open Mon–Sat 07:00–19:00 if a clock-in looks wrong before you export. The export sits on every plan, with the other four parts of the rota.

A setup session can enter your staff and patterns with you if you want that help. The session is 90 minutes and is a separate one-off, not part of the monthly price.

\ The demo is free /

Book a demo

pages.title: Prices
pages.content:
\ Per shop, per month /

Prices

Plans are priced per shop, in USD, and they exclude tax. The demo hour is free, and the first month on any plan after it is free as well.

\ Per shop, per month /

Plans

Prices per shop

First month free after the demo. Nothing is charged automatically. Cancel any month.

Prices per shop

Prices are in USD per shop, and they exclude tax. The demo hour is free. One shop, up to 15 staff, is $29 / month.

One shop, 16–40 staff, is $49 / month. One shop, 41–60 staff, is $69 / month. Each additional shop is $25 / month.

The setup session (90 minutes, we enter your staff and patterns) is $90 one-off. The paper-sheet import (we key in your last 4 weeks) is $60 one-off. First month free after the demo.

Nothing is charged automatically. Cancel any month. The staff bands sit inside the shops a demo suits: 5 to 60 staff, and 1 to 6 locations.

A second shop is the additional-shop price, not a second copy of the first band. The free month is the first month on any plan after the demo. It is not a reduced figure hiding inside the monthly price.

What every plan includes

Every plan includes the same five parts of the rota. You can lay out the week, collect availability, swap a shift, cover a sick day, and export hours for payroll. Staff read the published week on their own phones.

Support runs Mon–Sat 07:00–19:00, because many of these shops open before 08:00 and the early shift has already started when a usual office would. The week can be exported by Sunday night. The price changes with the number of staff in the shop, and with each additional shop.

It does not change because you use one part more than another. The setup session and the paper-sheet import sit outside the monthly plan. They are one-off, and you take them only if you want us to enter the staff, the patterns, or the last 4 weeks.

The demo hour itself is free, and it is not a plan.

The free month

The first month is free on any plan after the demo. Nothing is charged automatically. When the free month ends, the monthly price for your staff band applies only if you choose to continue.

Cancel any month. We reply to a booking within 1 working day, and after the demo a draft of your next week's rota arrives by email within 1 working day. That draft is part of the demo, not a charge.

The three slots are Mon–Fri at 10:00, 13:30 and 16:00, each 60 minutes, by video call, or at your shop if it is in Westmere. Office hours for the booking are Mon–Fri 08:30–17:30, on +1 555 0187 or demo@wariate-shifts.example. The free month does not start from a visit to the site, or from joining the early-access list.

It starts after the demo, on the plan you look at in the last ten minutes of the hour.

\ Billing /

Billing questions

What happens after the free month?

After the free month, the plan continues only if you want it to. The price is then the monthly band you already saw in the demo: $29 / month for one shop with up to 15 staff, $49 / month for 16–40 staff, or $69 / month for 41–60 staff, plus $25 / month for each additional shop. Tax is excluded.

Nothing is charged automatically at the end of the free month, so silence is not a purchase. Cancel any month, including the choice to stop as the free month finishes. The draft rota from the demo is already yours either way.

It was sent within 1 working day of the hour, and it does not depend on a card being stored. If your staff count moves into another band later, the monthly price moves to that band. The five parts of the rota stay the same on every band.

Is anything charged automatically?

Nothing is charged automatically. The demo hour is free. The first month on any plan after the demo is free, and that month does not roll into a paid month unless you choose to continue.

We do not take payment inside the booking form. Name, shop, staff count, preferred slot and email are there so we can reply within 1 working day and hold the hour. A photo of your current sheet is optional, and it is not a billing document.

The setup session at $90 one-off and the paper-sheet import at $60 one-off are agreed as separate pieces of work. They are not added because you booked a demo. Office hours for a question about a charge are Mon–Fri 08:30–17:30, on +1 555 0187 or demo@wariate-shifts.example.

Yusuf Demir looks after shop accounts from the office at 18 Coldharbour Yard.

Can we cancel any month?

Yes. Cancel any month. Plans are billed monthly, per shop, in USD, excluding tax.

There is no longer lock-in described in these prices. Stopping means the next month is not billed. You can cancel during the free month as well, and nothing is charged automatically if you do.

Cancelling does not delete the draft rota we already emailed after the demo. It stops the monthly plan. Support remains available through the paid month you are in, Mon–Sat 07:00–19:00.

A one-off that is already done, such as the 90-minute setup session or the import of your last 4 weeks, is the work of that session. It is not a monthly item, so cancelling the plan does not rewind it. If you want the plan again later, you book another conversation with the office and pick the band that matches your staff.

What is billed separately from the monthly plan?

Two pieces of work are one-off, and neither is required. The setup session is 90 minutes, and we enter your staff and patterns with you. It is $90 one-off.

The paper-sheet import is we key in your last 4 weeks. It is $60 one-off. The demo hour is free and is not one of these.

Lukas Brenner runs setup and onboarding, usually in a midday session on a working day. You can also do that entry yourself after the demo. The draft of next week, sent within 1 working day of the demo, is included in the hour and is not an import.

An import is four weeks of older sheets, keyed in so the pattern you copy forward is already there. Prices stay in USD. We do not convert them.

First month free after the demo. Nothing is charged automatically. Cancel any month.

\ The demo is free /

pages.title: Stories
pages.content:
\ Three shops, three weeks /

Stories

Three independent shops, three different weeks. The facts are the ones they run on: how many shops, how many staff, and who signs off the sheet.

1

Hollin Bakery

1 shop · 14 staff · opens 06:30

Hollin Bakery is 1 shop with 14 staff, and it opens at 06:30. Ines Duarte manages the floor. The weekend early shift used to be fixed on a Friday phone call, after the shop had closed and the sheet for Saturday was already pinned.

Someone would ring, someone would answer, and the name on the dawn start would change once more before morning. The call did the job, but it sat outside the week. The rest of the rota was on paper.

That one shift lived in a conversation. Staff now swap the early shift among themselves, and Ines approves once. A colleague offers the shift, another accepts, and the week does not change until Ines has said yes.

The 06:30 open stays covered by someone who already works the bakery. Ines still sees the offer and the acceptance together. The rest of the week is last week's pattern copied forward, people moved into the gaps, then published to phones and still readable on the wall.

Ines Duarte, manager, Hollin Bakery

2

Fennick Flowers

1 shop · 6 staff

Fennick Flowers is 1 shop with 6 staff. Oskar Lund is the manager. Wedding Saturdays need extra hands.

A Saturday wedding is not an ordinary weekend on the rota. The shop still has to open for people buying stems, and the back room is tying an order that cannot move to Monday. With six people, those Saturdays are the week that has to be decided first.

Availability for the season is collected in March, and the Saturdays are laid out first. Staff mark the days they can work. The Thursday reminder still goes out, and the answers land on the rota grid, but the question in March is the wedding season rather than a single week.

Once those Saturdays are filled, the ordinary weeks copy forward from the pattern around them. Oskar can see who is already committed to a wedding before he moves anyone into a weekday gap. Extra hands are people already on the staff who marked those Saturdays, not a separate list in a notebook.

Oskar Lund, manager, Fennick Flowers

3

Tessaly Books

2 shops · 11 staff

Tessaly Books is 2 shops with 11 staff. Ruth Adeyemi manages both. Some staff work at both shops.

A bookseller might shelve in one shop in the morning and cover the other after lunch. When each shop had its own sheet, the same person could be written onto both without anyone noticing until the day itself. One week shows both shops, so nobody is booked twice.

The additional shop sits on the same grid as the first. Ruth can see a name in both places before she publishes. A gap in one shop is filled only by someone who is free in that hour, not simply by someone who works for Tessaly Books in general.

Swaps still run between colleagues, and Ruth approves once. A sick day asks people who are free and able to work that shop. The hours for both shops add up on the same week, and the export by Sunday night covers people who moved between the two shops as well as people who stayed in one.

Ruth Adeyemi, manager, Tessaly Books

\ The demo is free /

pages.title: About
pages.content:
\ Westmere, since 2019 /

About

Wariate Shifts was founded in 2019 and works from the 2nd floor, 18 Coldharbour Yard, Westmere. The product is the week you already write, moved off a private sheet and onto the phones of the people who work it.

\ The office /

Founded in Westmere

Wariate Shifts was founded in 2019. The office is on the 2nd floor, 18 Coldharbour Yard, Westmere. It is rota software for independent shops: lay out the week, collect availability, swap shifts, cover sick days, and prepare hours for payroll.

The managers it is written for run 1 to 6 locations and 5 to 60 staff. Many of those shops open before 08:00, so the day here starts earlier than a typical desk. Support is open Mon–Sat 07:00–19:00.

The office itself can be reached Mon–Fri 08:30–17:30, on +1 555 0187 or at demo@wariate-shifts.example. A demo can be held at your shop if the shop is in Westmere. Everywhere else, the hour is a video call at 10:00, 13:30 or 16:00.

The product is the week on one sheet. The office is a single floor above Coldharbour Yard, and the people who answer are the seven named below.

Nine years of paper sheets

Hanna Rautio is co-founder, product. She ran a bakery floor for nine years before Wariate Shifts. The rota in those years was a paper sheet, written in pencil, copied forward when the week looked like the last one, and rewritten when it did not.

The early names had to be right before the shop opened. A phone call on Friday was sometimes the only way to fix a weekend start. She still treats the sheet as the object that already knows the week, and the copying as the part that wore people out.

The product follows that order. It starts by copying last week's pattern. It does not start by asking a manager to describe the shop in the abstract.

In the demo, the first ten minutes are that same question: how do you lay out the week now, on paper or in a spreadsheet? The next twenty-five minutes put that answer onto next week's grid.

\ The method /

Why it starts from paper

The product starts from paper because that is where the week already is. A spreadsheet counts as the same thing. Both are a grid of names and days that someone checked by eye.

Copy last week's pattern, drag people into the gaps, and publish to everyone's phone. Those three steps are the whole of laying out the week. Staff can keep a paper copy on the wall.

The phone view is the same week, not a second rota. Availability, swaps, sick days and hours sit on that grid afterwards. They do not ask you to rebuild it.

Tomás Aguilar, co-founder, engineering, builds those later changes so they land on the week you published, rather than in a separate list. A swap waits for your approval. The first yes on a sick day fills one open shift.

The Sunday export reads the hours, including breaks, from the week the floor worked.

\ The team /

The seven people

  • Hanna Rautio, co-founder, product
  • Tomás Aguilar, co-founder, engineering
  • Amara Okonkwo, demo lead
  • Lukas Brenner, setup and onboarding
  • Mei-Lin Ho, support, early shift
  • Rosa Ferreira, design
  • Yusuf Demir, shop accounts

There is no wider cast behind the names. A demo, a setup session, an early-morning support reply and a question about the bill all come back to this list. Portraits are not part of how we introduce them.

The work is the week, the hour, and the reply within 1 working day.

A day at Coldharbour Yard

The day starts at 07:00, when support opens for shops that open early. Mei-Lin Ho covers that early shift. The first demo is at 10:00.

Setup sessions run at midday: ninety minutes to enter staff and patterns. The 13:30 demo follows, then the 16:00 demo. Each demo is 60 minutes and has the same four parts.

Your week, then next week built from your sheet, then a live availability request, a swap and a sick day, then prices and questions. Draft rotas go out by email before 17:30. A booking is answered within 1 working day, and the draft after a demo is sent within 1 working day as well.

Office hours for a call are Mon–Fri 08:30–17:30. Support stays open until 19:00, and it is open on Saturday. The paper-sheet import is separate from the midday setup, and it is booked as its own one-off.

\ The demo is free /

Book a demo

pages.title: Book a demo
pages.content:
\ One hour, free /

Book a demo

Book a demo hour with Wariate Shifts. The hour is free, it runs for 60 minutes, and we reply within 1 working day.

\ Monday to Friday /

Book a demo

Book a demo

  • Minutes 0–10: your week, on paper or in a spreadsheet
  • Minutes 10–35: next week, built from your sheet
  • Minutes 35–50: an availability request, a swap and a sick day, live
  • Minutes 50–60: prices and questions

\ One hour, free /

The hour, in four parts

The slots are Mon–Fri at 10:00, 13:30 and 16:00. Each one is 60 minutes, by video call, or at your shop if it is in Westmere. The hour has four parts, and we keep them in this order.

Minutes 0–10 are your week: how you lay it out now, on paper or in a spreadsheet. Minutes 10–35 are build next week: we enter your real sheet together and lay out next week. Minutes 35–50 are changes: an availability request, a swap and a sick day, done live.

Minutes 50–60 are prices and questions: which plan fits, and what setup takes. After the demo, a draft of your next week's rota arrives by email within 1 working day. The demo hour is free.

The first month on any plan after the demo is free. Nothing is charged automatically. A photo of the current sheet is optional.

The paper-sheet import of your last 4 weeks is a later one-off, at $60, and it is not required for the hour.

What to send, and where we are

The booking asks for your name, your shop, your staff count, a preferred slot from 10:00, 13:30 or 16:00, and your email. Add a photo of your current sheet only if the pencil grid is easier to show than to describe. You can also call +1 555 0187 or write to demo@wariate-shifts.example.

Office hours are Mon–Fri 08:30–17:30. Support hours are Mon–Sat 07:00–19:00. The office is on the 2nd floor, 18 Coldharbour Yard, Westmere.

Amara Okonkwo is demo lead. If your shop is in Westmere, say so, and the hour can be at the shop rather than on a video call. We confirm within 1 working day.

The hour is not a setup session. Setup, if you want it afterwards, is 90 minutes with Lukas Brenner, entering your staff and patterns, at $90 one-off. Bring the sheet you use now.

We will use it from minute 10.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
\ What we collect /

Privacy

This note says what Wariate Shifts collects when you book a demo or join the early-access list, and what that message is used for. It stays with the fields on those forms.

What you send

A demo booking includes your name, your shop, your staff count, the slot you prefer from 10:00, 13:30 or 16:00, and your email. You may add a photo of your current sheet. That photo is optional, and the booking is complete without it.

An early-access note includes your name, your shop, the number of shops, and your email. If you call +1 555 0187, the office hears the number you call from during Mon–Fri 08:30–17:30. If you write, the message arrives at demo@wariate-shifts.example.

The form does not ask for a card number or a password. Staff names on a rota photo are there only because you chose to share the sheet for the draft of next week. Send what you are willing to have on the table during the hour.

The desk these messages reach is the 2nd floor, 18 Coldharbour Yard, Westmere.

What the office uses it for

We use a booking to reply within 1 working day, to hold a 60-minute demo, and to prepare the draft rota we email within 1 working day after the demo. The four parts of that hour are your current week, next week built from your sheet, the live changes, and prices. The photo, if you sent one, is read for that build.

It is not reused for another shop. We use an early-access note to write back about the multi-shop staff-sharing view, which is coming to all plans. Support may look at the same booking if you write during Mon–Sat 07:00–19:00 about the hour or the draft.

Shop accounts uses the shop name and the staff count only if, after the demo, you decide to take a monthly plan. Until then the details are for the demo and the draft. The first month is free after the demo.

Nothing is charged automatically. The booking form itself does not take payment.

What this page does not claim

This page describes the messages the office actually asks for. It does not add a certificate, a seal, or a count of records held. We do not ask you to create an account to book the hour.

The log-in link on the site returns you to the same demo booking. We do not ask for payment details in that form. Prices are discussed in minutes 50–60 of the demo, from the published bands, in USD, excluding tax.

If you would rather not send a photo of the sheet, bring it to the video call, or put it on the table if the demo is at your shop in Westmere. Questions about a booking you have already sent can go to demo@wariate-shifts.example or to +1 555 0187 in office hours, Mon–Fri 08:30–17:30. The people who handle demos, setup, early support and shop accounts are Amara Okonkwo, Lukas Brenner, Mei-Lin Ho and Yusuf Demir.

Terms

These terms cover the monthly plans, the free first month, cancellation, and the two one-off sessions. Amounts are USD per shop and exclude tax.

Plans billed monthly

Wariate Shifts is billed monthly, per shop, in USD, excluding tax. The demo hour is free. One shop, up to 15 staff, is $29 / month.

One shop, 16–40 staff, is $49 / month. One shop, 41–60 staff, is $69 / month. Each additional shop is $25 / month.

The bands are for shops with 5 to 60 staff and 1 to 6 locations, which is the audience the demo is built for. Every plan includes the same work: lay out the week, collect availability, swap a shift, cover a sick day, and hours for payroll. Staff read the week on their own phones.

Support is Mon–Sat 07:00–19:00. The week exports by Sunday night. The monthly price does not include the setup session or the paper-sheet import.

We do not show a converted price in another currency. A shop beyond 60 staff, or a site that needs a clinical overnight roster, is outside these plans.

The free month, and cancelling

The first month is free on any plan after the demo. Nothing is charged automatically. Cancel any month.

The free month begins after the demo, not when you first write to us, and not when you join the early-access list. We reply to a booking within 1 working day. Choosing a plan is part of minutes 50–60, when we look at which staff band fits and what setup takes.

If you do not take a plan, you are not enrolled, and no monthly amount is billed. If you continue after the free month, the price billed is the band you chose, excluding tax. Cancelling any month means the next month is not billed.

The draft rota emailed after the demo stays the draft we sent. It is not withdrawn because you cancel. These terms do not add a longer contract on top of the monthly plan.

The line under the prices is the whole of the trial: first month free after the demo, nothing charged automatically, cancel any month.

One-off work, and what the hours are not

The setup session is 90 minutes. We enter your staff and patterns. It is $90 one-off.

The paper-sheet import is we key in your last 4 weeks. It is $60 one-off. Neither is required to book the demo or to start a monthly plan.

Hours for payroll means clock in at the counter, breaks added up, and the week exported by Sunday night. That export is not a payroll system. It does not calculate pay, tax or deductions, and it does not replace the payroll you already use.

The demo is a video call, or at your shop if it is in Westmere, on a weekday at 10:00, 13:30 or 16:00. The office is on the 2nd floor, 18 Coldharbour Yard, Westmere. Phone +1 555 0187.

Email demo@wariate-shifts.example. Office hours are Mon–Fri 08:30–17:30. Support hours are Mon–Sat 07:00–19:00.

pages.content:

Thank you

Your note has reached Wariate Shifts. A person at the office will reply within 1 working day.

posts.title: What a paper rota gets right
posts.excerpt: A paper weekly sheet already holds the pattern of the shop, and the rota starts from that sheet rather than asking you to describe the week from nothing.
posts.content:
A paper rota is a weekly sheet on a clipboard, or pinned by the staff door, with names in pencil across the days. For a lot of independent shops it is still the clearest picture of the week. The person who wrote it knows who opens, who closes, and which part-timers can take a Thursday. Anyone walking past can read it. A change is a name rubbed out and written again. Before the shutters go up, the early shift can see it without unlocking a phone.

Wariate Shifts starts from that sheet. Laying out the week has three steps, and the first is to copy last week's pattern. The second is to drag people into the gaps the new week has opened. The third is to publish the same week to everyone's phone. A paper copy can still go on the wall. The point is not to retire the clipboard. The point is to stop the copying from being a private chore done after close, and to put the names where the people on them can read them.

Hanna Rautio, co-founder for product, ran a bakery floor for nine years. Those years were paper sheets, written before the ovens were really going, then rewritten when someone called in or swapped a Saturday. That is why the demo does not open with a tour. Minutes 0 to 10 are for how you lay the week out now, on paper or in a spreadsheet. Minutes 10 to 35 are for entering that real sheet together and laying out next week. You bring the grid you already trust. We do not hand you a blank one and ask you to invent the shop.

The sheet gets a few things right that are easy to lose once the week lives only in someone's head. It keeps one week in one place. It lets a calm week be a copy with small edits. And it stays in the room. Hollin Bakery opens at 06:30, with 14 staff in a single shop, and Ines Duarte still needs the early names to be settled before that open. A pinned week is there when the lights come on. Publishing to phones does not remove the wall copy. It means the same names are in the room and in the pocket, including for the person who is not yet on the floor.

What the paper sheet does less comfortably is the back-and-forth after it is pinned. A weekend early shift fixed on a Friday phone call. Availability scattered through a group chat. A sick day filled by ringing down a list while the shutters come up. Hours added up from memory on Sunday. Those jobs are the rest of the product, and they sit on the same grid rather than in a second book. Staff mark the days they can work. A reminder goes out on Thursday. Answers land on the rota grid. A colleague offers a shift, another accepts, and you approve once. For a sick day you mark the shift open, free and qualified people are asked, and the first yes fills it.

Hours are the part managers often do last, when the week is already a blur. Clock in at the counter. Breaks are added up. Export the week by Sunday night. The export is the hours the floor worked. It is not a payroll system, and it does not calculate pay, tax or deductions. Shops with 1 to 6 locations and 5 to 60 staff are the ones this is written for. A 24-hour site with a clinical roster, or a team looking to replace payroll, is outside it.

Fennick Flowers shows the other kind of paper problem. Oskar Lund has 1 shop and 6 staff, and wedding Saturdays need extra hands. He collects availability for the season in March and lays those Saturdays out first, before the ordinary weeks are filled. Tessaly Books is the two-shop version: Ruth Adeyemi, 2 shops, 11 staff, some people working in both. One week shows both, so nobody is booked twice. In each case the paper habit was already right. The missing piece was a single grid that could hold the exception without a side conversation.

If you want to try this on your own sheet, the demo is 60 minutes on a weekday, at 10:00, 13:30 or 16:00, by video call, or at your shop if it is in Westmere. The hour is free. Afterwards a draft of next week arrives by email within 1 working day. The first month on any plan is free after the demo, and nothing is charged automatically. Bring the pencil copy. It is still the best brief we can be given.

posts.title: Collecting availability without a group chat
posts.excerpt: Staff mark the days they can work, a reminder goes out on Thursday, and the answers land on the rota grid.
posts.content:
Availability used to arrive as scattered messages: a text on Sunday, a note at the till, a promise at the back door. By Thursday nobody was sure who had said what.

Now staff mark the days they can work on their own phone. A reminder goes out on Thursday, and the answers land on the rota grid, next to the shifts they affect.

You still lay out the week yourself. You just stop searching for the answers.

posts.title: Laying out a wedding season
posts.excerpt: Wedding Saturdays need extra hands. Collect availability in March and lay those Saturdays out first.
posts.content:
Wedding Saturdays need extra hands, and the extra hands need notice. A florist with six staff cannot find three more people on the Thursday before.

So the season's availability is collected in March, and the Saturdays are laid out first, before the ordinary weeks. The extra names come from people who have already said they can work.

The rest of the weeks fit around them.
